display: Paris hand bookbinder (11th arr.) making limited editions for collectors and small presses. I'm currently looking for about 4 metres of hand-dyed woven indigo silk for a 40-copy poetry edition.

signals.text: I need about 4 metres of woven silk, hand-dyed deep indigo, with a fine herringbone pattern, for a 40-copy poetry edition cover.
Every mill I've asked wants a 100-metre minimum, and I need 4. I'm looking for a small weaver or a sample workshop that will make a tiny run.
The cover has to be genuinely woven silk. Printed cloth, velvet and imitations won't do.
Mills in Lyon and Como both quoted 100 m minimums per colour, and neither would budge.
The finished copies are due to the collector in mid-February, and the cloth has to arrive well before then so I can bind. I'm getting nervous about the schedule.
I can pay up to about 180 euros per metre for the right cloth, and I'd happily pay more per metre to avoid buying 100.
I'm hunting for unusual cover cloth in flea markets, Marais fabric shops and online. I keep finding almost-right fabrics: faded indigo velvet, silk twill with no woven pattern.
I've been wondering whether an indigo-dyed silk could be commissioned from a dyer and a small hand-loom weaver working together.
I'm restoring a 1920s hotel guestbook with broken hinges. It's slow paste-and-patience work, and I'd like to talk to others who restore signed or autograph volumes.
I'm thinking about two-day beginner bookbinding workshops in the atelier this spring, and I'd like advice or a way to find participants.
I'd like to train my young assistant further, especially in layout, page order and finishing, so he stops making avoidable mistakes.
Atelier costs are rising in January, and I'm looking for steady income that doesn't depend on a single commission.

offers.text: Fine hand binding: full leather, half cloth, Coptic and Japanese stab, with rounded spines and linen thread.
Limited editions of 20–50 copies for collectors and small presses, made by hand. I don't do machine-made books.
Restoration of old bound volumes and hinge repair, using wheat paste and traditional methods.
A 38 m² Paris atelier in the 11th arrondissement with a 1930s lying press, a Schärfmaschine and Dutch bone folders. I can host small groups.
A network of about 20 collectors and small presses who send commissions. I can introduce a weaver, dyer or printer when there is a real fit.
Introductions to a gilder in Paris's 18th arrondissement and a marbler in Montreuil, both trusted collaborators.
A good eye for cover cloth and materials, plus knowledge of Paris suppliers for thread, leather and fabric. I can advise on which cloths bind well.
Mentoring a young apprentice: I teach sewing, paste work and finishing to someone who is learning fast.
Calf skin tanned in Annonay and similar leathers. I can share sourcing experience.
I volunteer weekly at a food bank in Paris, and I'm willing to help organise or connect people there.

catchers.hypo: Hello, I run a small hand-loom studio. We weave silk in short runs and could do a few metres in a custom herringbone, dyed indigo by a partner dyer.
catchers.can: I'd send the exact spec: 4 m, fine herringbone, deep indigo, 100% woven silk. I'd order samples, pay a fair price per metre, and credit the studio in the colophon.
catchers.confirm: Can you weave true silk (not a blend or print) in a fine herringbone, in a run of around 4 metres?

catchers.hypo: I'm a natural-dye artisan. I dye silk in indigo vats and often have undyed woven silk left over, with no minimum quantity.
catchers.can: I'd test dyeing silk samples and could pair you with a weaver if the base cloth is the problem.
catchers.confirm: Do you dye woven silk yardage by hand, in lengths of a few metres rather than bulk?

catchers.hypo: I work at a textile archive or deadstock reseller. We have remnants of woven silk, including indigo herringbone, in lengths of 2–10 metres.
catchers.can: I'd check the cloth against the spec (woven silk, herringbone, deep indigo, enough for 4 m in one piece) and buy it if it fits the 180 euros per metre budget.
catchers.confirm: Is the remnant genuinely woven silk (not printed, not velvet), in one continuous piece of at least 4 metres?

catchers.hypo: I'm a small press in Paris or Lyon. I print 30–100 copies and can't find a binder who works by hand and in small numbers.
catchers.can: I'd take on binding for small hand-bound runs, and refer larger or machine-made jobs elsewhere.
catchers.confirm: Is your edition a small run of under about 100 copies that you want bound by hand?

catchers.hypo: I'm a collector who inherited a damaged signed volume (guestbook, album or manuscript). It's fragile and I don't know who can repair it without harming it.
catchers.can: I'd assess the damage, advise on repair versus rebinding, and carry out the restoration.
catchers.confirm: Is the damage to the binding (hinges, spine, boards) rather than extensive water or mould damage?

catchers.hypo: I'm a young person who wants a craft trade. I'm looking for an atelier where I can learn bookbinding hands-on as an apprentice or intern.
catchers.can: I can't promise a post, but I'd talk about the atelier, point to training schools, and perhaps arrange a trial day or short workshop.
catchers.confirm: Are you looking to learn bookbinding by hand, and can you commit to regular time in Paris?

catchers.hypo: I'm an organiser of craft events or a cultural venue in Paris. I'd like a bookbinding workshop for beginners over a weekend.
catchers.can: I'd run a two-day beginner workshop in my atelier or at your venue, with materials and a bound book per participant.
catchers.confirm: Is the workshop for a small group (up to about 6 people) of beginners, over two days?

catchers.hypo: I'm a hotel or heritage owner with a historic register or guestbook that needs repair, and I'd like to keep its signatures and condition.
catchers.can: I'd do the work with period-appropriate methods, and I can introduce a gilder for the lettering.
catchers.confirm: Is the item a bound book that needs repair, rather than loose pages or a modern volume?

forbids.text: I don't make machine-made books or industrial runs.
I won't substitute printed or imitation cloth for the woven silk cover this edition requires.
The cloth must arrive early enough to bind before the mid-February delivery. Otherwise I'll have to renegotiate with the collector.
I won't pay beyond about 180 euros per metre for cover cloth.
I can't take binding work outside Paris on site. The atelier is in the 11th arrondissement.

projects.name: Forty-copy Occitan poetry edition, woven indigo silk cover
projects.text: A limited edition of a contemporary Occitan poet, letterpress-printed in Lyon and bound by hand in Paris for a Geneva collector. The cover is hand-dyed woven indigo silk with a fine herringbone, about 4 metres in total.

projects.name: Beginner bookbinding workshops in the atelier
projects.text: Two-day workshops for beginners in a 38 m² Paris atelier, planned for spring.

policy.t1: When there is a real lead on the cloth, I'll share the mill minimums I've met, my timeline (mid-February delivery), and my per-metre budget.
policy.t2: Once the match is strong and I know who I'm dealing with, I'll share atelier finances, such as costs and rent pressure.
policy.never: Nothing about my family or private life, including my children and my past relationships.
